audit_status.source_base: Greek Hebrews text tradition with Genesis 14 and Psalm 110 interpretation; draft aligned to public-domain comparison layer later
audit_status.review_note: Compact complete draft reviewed for Melchizedek, Abraham tithe, Levi, change of priesthood, indestructible life, better hope, permanent priesthood.

verses.restored: For this Melchizedek, king of Salem, priest of Most High Divine, meeting Abraham returning from slaughter of kings and blessing him,

familiar.text: For this Melchisedec, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him;

modern.text: This Melchizedek was king of Salem and priest of God Most High. He met Abraham returning from the slaughter of the kings and blessed him,

original.text: Οὗτος γὰρ ὁ Μελχισέδεκ, βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ἱερεὺς τοῦ θεοῦ τοῦ ὑψίστου, ⸀ὁ συναντήσας Ἀβραὰμ ὑποστρέφοντι ἀπὸ τῆς κοπῆς τῶν βασιλέων καὶ εὐλογήσας αὐτόν,

verses.restored: to whom also Abraham apportioned a tenth from all, first being interpreted king of righteousness/justice, and then also king of Salem, which is king of peace,

familiar.text: To whom also Abraham gave a tenth part of all; first being by interpretation King of righteousness, and after that also King of Salem, which is, King of peace;

modern.text: and Abraham apportioned to him a tenth of everything. First, his name means “king of righteousness.” Then also, “king of Salem” means “king of peace.”

original.text: ᾧ καὶ δεκάτην ἀπὸ πάντων ἐμέρισεν Ἀβραάμ, πρῶτον μὲν ἑρμηνευόμενος βασιλεὺς δικαιοσύνης ἔπειτα δὲ καὶ βασιλεὺς Σαλήμ, ὅ ἐστιν βασιλεὺς εἰρήνης,

verses.restored: without father, without mother, without genealogy, having neither beginning of days nor end of life, but being made like the Son of the Divine, remains priest continually.

familiar.text: Without father, without mother, without descent, having neither beginning of days, nor end of life; but made like unto the Son of God; abideth a priest continually.

modern.text: Without father or mother or genealogy, without beginning of days or end of life, like the Son of God, he remains a priest for all time.

original.text: ἀπάτωρ, ἀμήτωρ, ἀγενεαλόγητος, μήτε ἀρχὴν ἡμερῶν μήτε ζωῆς τέλος ἔχων, ἀφωμοιωμένος δὲ τῷ υἱῷ τοῦ θεοῦ, μένει ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸ διηνεκές.

verses.restored: Now see how great this one is, to whom Abraham the patriarch gave a tenth from the best spoils.

familiar.text: Now consider how great this man was, unto whom even the patriarch Abraham gave the tenth of the spoils.

modern.text: Consider how great Melchizedek was: Even the patriarch Abraham gave him a tenth of the plunder.

original.text: Θεωρεῖτε δὲ πηλίκος οὗτος ⸀ᾧ δεκάτην Ἀβραὰμ ἔδωκεν ἐκ τῶν ἀκροθινίων ὁ πατριάρχης.

verses.restored: And those from sons of Levi receiving priesthood have command according to Law to take tithes from the people, that is, from their siblings, though these have come out of Abraham's loins.

familiar.text: And verily they that are of the sons of Levi, who receive the office of the priesthood, have a commandment to take tithes of the people according to the law, that is, of their brethren, though they come out of the loins of Abraham:

modern.text: Now the law commands the sons of Levi who become priests to collect a tenth from the people—that is, from their brothers—though they too are descended from Abraham.

original.text: καὶ οἱ μὲν ἐκ τῶν υἱῶν Λευὶ τὴν ἱερατείαν λαμβάνοντες ἐντολὴν ἔχουσιν ἀποδεκατοῦν τὸν λαὸν κατὰ τὸν νόμον, τοῦτʼ ἔστιν τοὺς ἀδελφοὺς αὐτῶν, καίπερ ἐξεληλυθότας ἐκ τῆς ὀσφύος Ἀβραάμ·

verses.restored: But the one not tracing genealogy from them received tithes from Abraham and blessed the one having the promises.

familiar.text: But he whose descent is not counted from them received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him that had the promises.

modern.text: But Melchizedek, who did not trace his descent from Levi, collected a tenth from Abraham and blessed him who had the promises.

original.text: ὁ δὲ μὴ γενεαλογούμενος ἐξ αὐτῶν δεδεκάτωκεν ⸀Ἀβραάμ, καὶ τὸν ἔχοντα τὰς ἐπαγγελίας εὐλόγηκεν.

verses.restored: And without all dispute, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

familiar.text: And without all contradiction the less is blessed of the better.

modern.text: And indisputably, the lesser is blessed by the greater.

original.text: χωρὶς δὲ πάσης ἀντιλογίας τὸ ἔλαττον ὑπὸ τοῦ κρείττονος εὐλογεῖται.

verses.restored: And here dying humans receive tithes, but there one testified that he lives.

familiar.text: And here men that die receive tithes; but there he receiveth them, of whom it is witnessed that he liveth.

modern.text: In the case of the Levites, mortal men collect the tenth; but in the case of Melchizedek, it is affirmed that he lives on.

original.text: καὶ ὧδε μὲν δεκάτας ἀποθνῄσκοντες ἄνθρωποι λαμβάνουσιν, ἐκεῖ δὲ μαρτυρούμενος ὅτι ζῇ.

verses.restored: And so to speak, through Abraham even Levi, the one receiving tithes, has paid tithes,

familiar.text: And as I may so say, Levi also, who receiveth tithes, payed tithes in Abraham.

modern.text: And so to speak, Levi, who collects the tenth, paid the tenth through Abraham.

original.text: καὶ ὡς ἔπος εἰπεῖν, διʼ Ἀβραὰμ καὶ Λευὶ ὁ δεκάτας λαμβάνων δεδεκάτωται,

verses.restored: for he was still in the loins of the father when Melchizedek met him.

familiar.text: For he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedec met him.

modern.text: For when Melchizedek met Abraham, Levi was still in the loin of his ancestor. A Superior Priesthood

original.text: ἔτι γὰρ ἐν τῇ ὀσφύϊ τοῦ πατρὸς ἦν ὅτε συνήντησεν αὐτῷ ⸀Μελχισέδεκ.

verses.restored: Therefore if completion were through the Levitical priesthood, for upon it the people received Law, what further need was there for another priest to arise according to order of Melchizedek and not be named according to order of Aaron?

familiar.text: If therefore perfection were by the Levitical priesthood, (for under it the people received the law,) what further need was there that another priest should rise after the order of Melchisedec, and not be called after the order of Aaron?

modern.text: Now if perfection could have been attained through the Levitical priesthood (for on this basis the people received the law), why was there still need for another priest to appear—one in the order of Melchizedek and not in the order of Aaron?

original.text: Εἰ μὲν οὖν τελείωσις διὰ τῆς Λευιτικῆς ἱερωσύνης ἦν, ὁ λαὸς γὰρ ἐπʼ ⸀αὐτῆς ⸀νενομοθέτηται, τίς ἔτι χρεία κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ ἕτερον ἀνίστασθαι ἱερέα καὶ οὐ κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Ἀαρὼν λέγεσθαι;

verses.restored: For priesthood being changed, of necessity there is also change of Law.

familiar.text: For the priesthood being changed, there is made of necessity a change also of the law.

modern.text: For when the priesthood is changed, the law must be changed as well.

original.text: μετατιθεμένης γὰρ τῆς ἱερωσύνης ἐξ ἀνάγκης καὶ νόμου μετάθεσις γίνεται.

verses.restored: For the one of whom these things are said has shared in another tribe, from which no one has attended the altar.

familiar.text: For he of whom these things are spoken pertaineth to another tribe, of which no man gave attendance at the altar.

modern.text: He of whom these things are said belonged to a different tribe, from which no one has ever served at the altar.

original.text: ἐφʼ ὃν γὰρ λέγεται ταῦτα φυλῆς ἑτέρας μετέσχηκεν, ἀφʼ ἧς οὐδεὶς προσέσχηκεν τῷ θυσιαστηρίῳ·

verses.restored: For it is evident that our Lord has arisen from Judah, concerning which tribe Moses spoke nothing about priests.

familiar.text: For it is evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda; of which tribe Moses spake nothing concerning priesthood.

modern.text: For it is clear that our Lord descended from Judah, a tribe as to which Moses said nothing about priests.

original.text: πρόδηλον γὰρ ὅτι ἐξ Ἰούδα ἀνατέταλκεν ὁ κύριος ἡμῶν, εἰς ἣν φυλὴν ⸂περὶ ἱερέων οὐδὲν⸃ Μωϋσῆς ἐλάλησεν.

verses.restored: And it is still more abundantly clear if another priest arises according to likeness of Melchizedek,

familiar.text: And it is yet far more evident: for that after the similitude of Melchisedec there ariseth another priest,

modern.text: And this point is even more clear if another priest like Melchizedek appears,

original.text: Καὶ περισσότερον ἔτι κατάδηλόν ἐστιν, εἰ κατὰ τὴν ὁμοιότητα Μελχισέδεκ ἀνίσταται ἱερεὺς ἕτερος,

verses.restored: who has become so not according to Law of fleshly commandment, but according to power of indestructible life.

familiar.text: Who is made, not after the law of a carnal commandment, but after the power of an endless life.

modern.text: one who has become a priest not by a law of succession, but by the power of an indestructible life.

original.text: ὃς οὐ κατὰ νόμον ἐντολῆς ⸀σαρκίνης γέγονεν ἀλλὰ κατὰ δύναμιν ζωῆς ἀκαταλύτου,

verses.restored: For it is testified: You are priest into the age according to order of Melchizedek.

familiar.text: For he testifieth, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec.

modern.text: For it is testified: “You are a priest forever in the order of Melchizedek.”

original.text: ⸀μαρτυρεῖται γὰρ ὅτι Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα κατὰ τὴν τάξιν Μελχισέδεκ.

verses.restored: For on one hand there is setting aside of preceding command because of its weakness and unprofitability,

familiar.text: For there is verily a disannulling of the commandment going before for the weakness and unprofitableness thereof.

modern.text: So the former commandment is set aside because it was weak and useless

original.text: ἀθέτησις μὲν γὰρ γίνεται προαγούσης ἐντολῆς διὰ τὸ αὐτῆς ἀσθενὲς καὶ ἀνωφελές,

verses.restored: for Law completed nothing, but there is bringing in of better hope through which we draw near to the Divine.

familiar.text: For the law made nothing perfect, but the bringing in of a better hope did; by the which we draw nigh unto God.

modern.text: (for the law made nothing perfect), and a better hope is introduced, by which we draw near to God.

original.text: οὐδὲν γὰρ ἐτελείωσεν ὁ νόμος, ἐπεισαγωγὴ δὲ κρείττονος ἐλπίδος, διʼ ἧς ἐγγίζομεν τῷ θεῷ.

verses.restored: And inasmuch as not apart from oath—others indeed have become priests without oath,

familiar.text: And inasmuch as not without an oath he was made priest:

modern.text: And none of this happened without an oath. For others became priests without an oath,

original.text: Καὶ καθʼ ὅσον οὐ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας (οἱ μὲν γὰρ χωρὶς ὁρκωμοσίας εἰσὶν ἱερεῖς γεγονότες,

verses.restored: but he with oath through the One saying to him: Lord swore and will not change mind: You are priest into the age—

familiar.text: (For those priests were made without an oath; but this with an oath by him that said unto him, The Lord sware and will not repent, Thou art a priest for ever after the order of Melchisedec:)

modern.text: but Jesus became a priest with an oath by the One who said to Him: “The Lord has sworn and will not change His mind: ‘You are a priest forever.’”

original.text: ὁ δὲ μετὰ ὁρκωμοσίας διὰ τοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς αὐτόν· Ὤμοσεν κύριος, καὶ οὐ μεταμεληθήσεται, Σὺ ἱερεὺς εἰς τὸν ⸀αἰῶνα),

verses.restored: by so much also Jesus has become guarantor of better covenant.

familiar.text: By so much was Jesus made a surety of a better testament.

modern.text: Because of this oath, Jesus has become the guarantee of a better covenant.

original.text: κατὰ ⸀τοσοῦτο ⸀κρείττονος διαθήκης γέγονεν ἔγγυος Ἰησοῦς.

verses.restored: And the many have become priests because they are hindered by death from remaining,

familiar.text: And they truly were many priests, because they were not suffered to continue by reason of death:

modern.text: Now there have been many other priests, since death prevented them from continuing in office.

original.text: Καὶ οἱ μὲν πλείονές εἰσιν γεγονότες ἱερεῖς διὰ τὸ θανάτῳ κωλύεσθαι παραμένειν·

verses.restored: but this one, because he remains into the age, holds priesthood untransferable/permanent.

familiar.text: But this man, because he continueth ever, hath an unchangeable priesthood.

modern.text: But because Jesus lives forever, He has a permanent priesthood.

original.text: ὁ δὲ διὰ τὸ μένειν αὐτὸν εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα ἀπαράβατον ἔχει τὴν ἱερωσύνην·

verses.restored: Therefore he is able to save/heal completely those drawing near to the Divine through him, always living to intercede on their behalf.

familiar.text: Wherefore he is able also to save them to the uttermost that come unto God by him, seeing he ever liveth to make intercession for them.

modern.text: Therefore He is able to save completely those who draw near to God through Him, since He always lives to intercede for them.

original.text: ὅθεν καὶ σῴζειν εἰς τὸ παντελὲς δύναται τοὺς προσερχομένους διʼ αὐτοῦ τῷ θεῷ, πάντοτε ζῶν εἰς τὸ ἐντυγχάνειν ὑπὲρ αὐτῶν.

verses.restored: For such high priest was fitting for us: holy, harmless, undefiled, separated from sinners/misaligned ones, and become higher than heavens,

familiar.text: For such an high priest became us, who is holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens;

modern.text: Such a high priest truly befits us—One who is holy, innocent, undefiled, set apart from sinners, and exalted above the heavens.

original.text: Τοιοῦτος γὰρ ἡμῖν ⸀καὶ ἔπρεπεν ἀρχιερεύς, ὅσιος, ἄκακος, ἀμίαντος, κεχωρισμένος ἀπὸ τῶν ἁμαρτωλῶν, καὶ ὑψηλότερος τῶν οὐρανῶν γενόμενος·

verses.restored: who does not have daily necessity, like the high priests, first to offer sacrifices for own sins/misalignments and then for those of people; for this he did once for all, offering himself.

familiar.text: Who needeth not daily, as those high priests, to offer up sacrifice, first for his own sins, and then for the people’s: for this he did once, when he offered up himself.

modern.text: Unlike the other high priests, He does not need to offer daily sacrifices, first for His own sins and then for the sins of the people; He sacrificed for sin once for all when He offered up Himself.

original.text: ὃς οὐκ ἔχει καθʼ ἡμέραν ἀνάγκην, ὥσπερ οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς, πρότερον ὑπὲρ τῶν ἰδίων ἁμαρτιῶν θυσίας ἀναφέρειν, ἔπειτα τῶν τοῦ λαοῦ (τοῦτο γὰρ ἐποίησεν ἐφάπαξ ἑαυτὸν ἀνενέγκας)·

verses.restored: For Law appoints humans as high priests having weakness, but word of oath after the Law appoints Son, completed into the age.

familiar.text: For the law maketh men high priests which have infirmity; but the word of the oath, which was since the law, maketh the Son, who is consecrated for evermore.

modern.text: For the law appoints as high priests men who are weak; but the oath, which came after the law, appointed the Son, who has been made perfect forever.

original.text: ὁ νόμος γὰρ ἀνθρώπους καθίστησιν ἀρχιερεῖς ἔχοντας ἀσθένειαν, ὁ λόγος δὲ τῆς ὁρκωμοσίας τῆς μετὰ τὸν νόμον υἱόν, εἰς τὸν αἰῶνα τετελειωμένον.

translation_notes: Melchizedek is interpreted through name, genealogy absence, and Psalm 110; avoid speculative mythology beyond the argument.
Change of priesthood/law is a Hebrews-internal cultic argument, not a rejection of Jewish people or Scripture.
Jesus' priesthood is grounded in indestructible life and ongoing intercession.
safety_note: Do not weaponize 'weakness/unprofitability' language as contempt for Torah or Judaism; Hebrews argues about priestly completion and access to Divine, using Scripture itself.
